chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Durusta al-Wasiti, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The marriage of the People of the Book is not proper (or: is not permissible). I said: 'I am your ransom, where is its prohibition?' He said: 'His saying, Exalted is He: Do not hold the ties of the disbelievers [in marriage].'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on marrying People of the Book according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that while marriage to the People of the Book is not strictly prohibited (*haram*), it is legally discouraged (*la yanbaghi*) due to potential religious compromise. He substantiates this by citing the Quranic command 'do not hold the ties of the disbelievers' (2:221), interpreting 'ties' (*ismam*) specifically as the enduring marital bond. This reflects the Shia juristic view that such unions are permissible but inferior to marrying a Muslim woman, prioritizing the preservation of faith within the household.
